newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end stronger with SMI up 3.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end stronger with SMI up 3.2 pct.

text.p: Swiss shares recovered on Tuesday from losses the day before, gaining over three percent on the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI).
Dealers said positive U.S. financial markets on Monday, Wall Street's firm opening on Tuesday and derivatives-related buying supported the market.
The correction on the Swsis market seemed to be over, one dealer said.
SMI advanced 174.5 points or 3.23 percent to reach 5,580.1 points.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index rose 94.09 points or 2.69 percent to close at 3,586.10.
The market was also supported by a stronger dollar and growing optimism that German and U.S. interest rates might not rise, despite earlier speculation of rate moves.
Dealers said share prices might drop a little on Wednesday in profit-taking after the day's gains.
Chemicals and pharma shares profited from the recovery.
Novartis, which was most traded, rose 117 francs to 2,252. Roche advanced 285 francs to close at 13,600. Clariant rose 55 francs to 1,064. Ciba jumped 8.25 francs to 138.
Industrials like Oerlikon and Sulzer were also stronger.

Oerlikon rose nine francs to 168. The share profited from hopes that Ernst Thomke, head of shoes and fashion division Bally, would not resign after a meeting with the Oerlikon board on Monday ended with no news.
Registered shares of Sulzer jumped 15 francs to 1,170. Holderbank were 3.41 percent higher at 1,273 francs.
UBS rose 1.83 percent to 1,500 and SBC advanced 4.50 francs to close at 393.
Shares of CS Group were a clear market outperformer, rising 4.97 percent to 190 francs.
Traders said there was speculation of a future link-up between CS group and Germany's Commerzbank.
The speculation was based on rumors that Swiss shareholder activist Martin Ebner held 15 percent of Commerzebank. Ebner's BZ Group to declined to comment.

According to the speculation, Ebner would use his Commerzbank stake to force some kind of alliance with the CS Group after CS's planned merger with Winterthur, which would make Ebner a major shareholder in CS Group.
